content: Torsemide is a diuretic, commonly referred to as a water pill, that is prescribed to alleviate swelling and fluid retention caused by conditions such as heart or liver disease. The medication works by prompting the kidneys to excrete excess water and salt into the urine. In some cases, torsemide may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Torsemide is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically once daily in the morning. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely. If you have any questions or need clarification, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Take torsemide exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not discontinue use without consulting your doctor. Before starting torsemide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to torsemide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications.g., prednisone), digoxin (Lanoxin), indomethacin (Indocin), lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid), probenecid (Benemid), or vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Do not breastfeed while taking torsemide. If you become pregnant while on this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, if you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking torsemide. Follow your doctor’s dietary recommendations, which may include a low-sodium or low-salt diet, potassium supplements, and increased consumption of potassium-rich foods such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice. Your doctor may also recommend a daily exercise regimen. If you miss a dose of torsemide, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Common side effects of torsemide include frequent urination, which may persist for up to six hours after taking a dose but should decrease after a few weeks of use. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: muscle cramps, weakness, dizziness, faintness, fatigue, headache, confusion, thirst, upset stomach, or vomiting. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. Contact your doctor if you experience rapid and excessive weight loss or if you vomit blood. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store torsemide in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. The brand name for torsemide is Demadex Oral®.
